name: CJC/IPA Protocol

lead: CJC/IPA combines CJC-1295 with ipamorelin, two peptides that prompt the body to release more growth hormone. People use it hoping for more muscle, a leaner look and faster recovery.

CJC-1295 mimics growth-hormone-releasing hormone and ipamorelin activates the ghrelin receptor; together they raise growth hormone and IGF-1, which feed recovery, muscle and fat metabolism. No trial has tested the pair for appearance. The two were studied separately: CJC-1295 reached phase II before research stopped, and ipamorelin did not pass a phase II trial for postoperative ileus.

paras: It is discussed in forums and peptide circles as a stack that users buy as research peptides and run for body-composition goals alongside training and diet. Users describe changes in recovery and body composition building over weeks to months.

CJC-1295 research was stopped after a participant died, which the physician attributed to unrelated coronary disease. Users report water retention, including in the face and around the eyes, and forum threads ask about effects in teenagers' growth plates. Neither compound is approved, both are sold as research peptides, and both are on the WADA prohibited list.

angle.text: CJC/IPA raises growth hormone release, which raises IGF-1 and supports recovery, so users aim for more muscle and a leaner look. Forum users also mention water retention changing the face and eyes; the pair has not been tested in a trial.

lead: CJC/IPA refers to the combined use of CJC-1295, a long-acting analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH), and ipamorelin, a selective ghrelin-receptor (growth hormone secretagogue) agonist, both aimed at raising growth hormone (GH) release [1][2]. Neither is an approved drug.

On looksmax.org, the pairing is discussed by users who buy it as research peptides, with threads about side effects such as facial water retention and about whether it affects growth plates in teenagers [3][4].

No published trial has tested the combination for appearance outcomes. The two compounds were studied separately: CJC-1295 reached phase II trials before research was stopped, and ipamorelin failed a phase II trial for postoperative ileus [1][2].
infobox: Both on the WADA prohibited list [1][2]

paras: CJC-1295 is a modified GHRH(1-29) fragment; the DAC version binds albumin, giving an estimated half-life of 6 to 8 days in humans [1]. Studies reported raised GH and IGF-1 after single doses [1]. It was investigated for lipodystrophy and GH deficiency; research was terminated as a precaution after the death of a phase II participant, which the attending physician attributed to likely asymptomatic coronary artery disease [1].

Ipamorelin is a pentapeptide derived from GHRP-1 with an elimination half-life of about 2 hours that raises GH without reported effects on prolactin, FSH, LH, TSH, ACTH or cortisol [2]. Helsinn tested it for postoperative ileus and the program was discontinued for lack of efficacy [2].

Ipamorelin is commonly marketed as a research peptide rather than an approved drug, and athletes have used it; both compounds are on the WADA prohibited list [1][2]. Forum users describe ordering from overseas suppliers [5].

Users report water retention and changes in eye appearance after starting the pair [3]. A teenager asked whether the stack could close growth plates early or limit height; replies were brief and unreferenced [4]. No studies on this question were found.
No studies found on the combination. Separately, CJC-1295 raised GH and IGF-1 in early human studies [1], and ipamorelin raised GH in volunteers but did not show efficacy for postoperative ileus [2].
